title: Glacier National Park Trip Planner Printable, Going-to-the-Sun Road Itinerary, Logan Pass Shuttle Guide, Best Day Hikes, Montana Travel PDF
description:
Planning a first trip to Glacier National Park? This 30-page printable guide puts the whole trip on paper: when Going-to-the-Sun Road opens, what changed for 2026 (no vehicle reservations, the ticketed Logan Pass shuttle and the 3-hour parking limit), what to book and in what order, and how to spend 2, 3 or 5 days.

WHAT'S INSIDE
- The park at a glance: Lake McDonald, Logan Pass, St. Mary, Many Glacier, Two Medicine and the North Fork, with drive times in miles and km
- When to go, month by month, and why the high road has no fixed opening date
- Entry and passes: 2026 fees, annual passes, and what to do if an area is full and cars are diverted
- Logan Pass: shuttle ticket or 3-hour permit, boarding places, ticket release times and the last bus back
- What to book and when: lodging, gateway towns, campgrounds, boat tours and shuttle tickets
- Bears and wildlife (bear spray, safe distances, food storage), snow on trails into July, cold water and fast weather
- Going-to-the-Sun Road stop by stop, with vehicle size limits
- Sample 2-day, 3-day and 5-day plans, with swaps for when the road is not open yet
- 12 day hikes, from Trail of the Cedars and Avalanche Lake to Hidden Lake Overlook, the Highline, Grinnell Lake and Iceberg Lake, with distance in mi and km and climb in ft and m, from NPS figures
- Rainy-day ideas, a day in Waterton Lakes, packing list, trip budget, day-by-day planner, bookings log and notes

WHAT YOU GET
- US Letter and A4 versions
- Mobile edition, sized for reading on your phone
- Color and printer-friendly (low ink) versions
- Instant download. This is a digital file; nothing is shipped.
- Bonus: our free one-page Ultimate Hiking Checklist

GOOD TO KNOW
Checked against nps.gov in November 2026. Glacier changes its access rules, shuttles, fees and closures from year to year, so check the official park website for your dates before you book. No maps or GPS files. Not affiliated with the National Park Service. For personal use.

Made by HikeSupply Co., a small shop for weekend hikers. More printable hiking guides in our Etsy shop.
